title: The direct image of a coherent module along a finite morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme is coherent
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] with $X$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent] (for instance $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_Y$). Then $f_*\mathcal F$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module; for every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$, with $f^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $(f_*\mathcal F)(U)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}U)$ is a finite $R$-module. (Stacks' statement also gives $R^pf_*\mathcal F=0$ for $p>0$; that part is not stated here.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y6 (lemma-finite-pushforward-coherent), coherence part, with Lemma 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian)

proof.text: *Step 1 (f over an affine open).* Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ be an affine open. Since $f$ is finite it is affine and $f^{-1}(U)$ is affine, $f^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B=\mathcal O_Y(f^{-1}U)$, and the ring map $\varphi=f^\sharp_U:R\to B$ is finite: $B$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. (This is the definition applied to $U$.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y6 (lemma-finite-pushforward-coherent, line 2455), proof: 'By Morphisms, Definition 01WH we see that f^{-1}(V)=Spec(B) with A -> B finite'

proof.text: *Step 2 (F is quasi-coherent of finite type).* $\mathcal F$ is of finite type by the definition of coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. It is moreover of finite presentation: given $y\in Y$, choose an open $W\ni y$ and a surjection $\Psi:\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_W$ (finite type); by the second condition of coherence $\ker\Psi$ is of finite type, so there are an open $y\in V\subseteq W$ and a surjection $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to(\ker\Psi)|_V$; the composite $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\Psi|_V}\mathcal F|_V\to0$ is exact (exactness of sheaves restricted to $V$ is checked on the same sheaves), which is a finite presentation of $\mathcal F$ near $y$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. Hence $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](0).

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BW (lemma-coherent-finite-presentation, line 1596) and its proof; Lemma 01BO (lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-coherent) for quasi-coherence; cited in the proof of Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01XZ, (1)=>(2)

proof.text: *Step 3 (sections over the affine preimage).* With $U$, $B$ as in Step 1, put $M=\mathcal F(f^{-1}U)$. The restriction $\mathcal F|_{f^{-1}U}$ is quasi-coherent of finite type (Step 2; both properties are local, so they pass to the open subscheme $f^{-1}U$), and $f^{-1}U$ is affine with $\mathcal O_Y(f^{-1}U)=B$; by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a) $M$ is a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PB (lemma-finite-type-module, line 2093), as used in the proof of Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01XZ ((2)=>(4)) and of Lemma 01Y6

proof.text: *Step 4 (the sections of f_*F over U are a finite R-module).* By definition of the direct image of modules along $f$ [def-pc-module-pullback], $(f_*\mathcal F)(U)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}U)=M$, with $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$ acting through $\varphi=f^\sharp_U:R\to B$. Since $B$ is a finitely generated $R$-module (Step 1) and $M$ a finitely generated $B$-module (Step 3), $M$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-over-finite-algebra]. This is the second assertion of the statement.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y6 (lemma-finite-pushforward-coherent, line 2455), proof: 'If M is a finite B-module, then M is also finite viewed as an A-module, see Algebra, Lemma 00GJ'

proof.text: *Step 5 (f_*F is quasi-coherent).* $f$ is affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent (Step 2), so $f_*\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](1).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y6 (lemma-finite-pushforward-coherent, line 2455), proof (a finite morphism is affine, by definition); Schemes, Lemma 01LC for the quasi-coherence of the direct image

proof.text: *Step 6 (f_*F is of finite type).* Cover $X$ by affine opens $U_j$ [def-pc-scheme]. By Step 4, $(f_*\mathcal F)(U_j)$ is a finitely generated $\mathcal O_X(U_j)$-module for every $j$, and $f_*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent (Step 5); hence $f_*\mathcal F$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](c).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y6 (lemma-finite-pushforward-coherent, line 2455), proof, via Lemma 01XZ ((5)=>(2)): quasi-coherent with finite modules on an affine open covering

proof.text: *Step 7 (f_*F is coherent).* $X$ is locally Noetherian and $f_*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type (Steps 5, 6), so $f_*\mathcal F$ is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. With Step 4 this proves the statement for coherent $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian, line 2225), (2)=>(1), as invoked in the proof of Lemma 01Y6

proof.text: *Step 8 (the example F = O_Y is coherent).* $Y$ is locally Noetherian: by [pqf-def-locnoeth] choose an affine open covering $X=\bigcup_iU_i$, $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ with $R_i$ Noetherian; by Step 1, $f^{-1}(U_i)=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ with $B_i$ a finitely generated $R_i$-module, so $B_i$ is a Noetherian ring [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian], and the affine opens $f^{-1}(U_i)$ cover $Y$, so $Y$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. The module $\mathcal O_Y$ is of finite presentation (the sequence $\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus0}\to\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus1}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\mathcal O_Y\to0$ is exact), hence quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](0), and of finite type (the identity $\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_Y$ is a surjection) [pqf-def-coherent]; so $\mathcal O_Y$ is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] on the locally Noetherian $Y$, and Steps 1-7 apply to $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_Y$.

split_report.summary: Proof written in 8 steps following Stacks 01Y6 with 01XZ: finite => affine with R -> B finite (definition); coherent => finite presentation => quasi-coherent of finite type (Modules 01BW written out, then (0) of lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine), so F(f^{-1}U) is a finite B-module ((a) of that node), hence a finite R-module (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-over-finite-algebra, Module.Finite.trans, Stacks 00GJ); f_*F quasi-coherent by lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change(1) (same unit, instead of pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh), of finite type by (c), coherent by pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth (01XZ). The statement's parenthetical 'for instance F = O_Y' needs Y locally Noetherian; Step 8 proves it (Y locally Noetherian via new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian, IsNoetherianRing.of_finite; O_Y finitely presented, hence quasi-coherent of finite type, hence coherent by 01XZ). Statement kept; def-pc-module-pullback added to stmt_deps (the module functors f_*, f^*). pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth is in unit sk-prop-av-pqf-finite (outside the route of sk-thm-p1): used as a generic tool lemma (01XZ).
